adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` defines computed keys as `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. These are evaluated immediately as plain JS property names; `z.string()` is an object, so `.toString()` will not create a dynamic “any string key” and instead produces a single literal key (and both computed keys collide). As a result, when the “minimum” schema is used (when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set), Zod will strip real token fields like `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, `instance_url`, etc., leaving essentially only `access_token` (plus the artificially injected `refresh_token`). This matches the downstream breakage described: Office365 won’t update expiry, Zoom/Salesforce would lose required fields when the minimal schema path is taken.
